alternative_architecture.description: Replace the milestone-platform plan with a thin vertical-slice delivery coordinator. State: stable requirement IDs/revisions in the GDD, small Git-versioned task contracts, one local SQLite/event journal for transient execution, Git commits as implementation truth, immutable external validation manifests, and GitHub as a rebuildable projection only. Planning: keep a rolling three-to-five-item frontier chosen by the human; decompose only the selected slice. Execution: one write-capable agent in one branch/worktree. Validation: deterministic Git checks, Windows Unity compile/EditMode/PlayMode runs, one semantic diff review, then human experiential review. Recovery: explicit compare-and-set transitions with idempotency keys—planned, claimed, workspace_ready, implemented, validating, needs_human, merge_ready, merged, verified—and reconciliation against actual Git refs/PR state after restart. GDD changes: diff stable requirement revisions and invalidate only referencing tasks/evidence plus affected dependents. Unity integration: one Windows host adapter owns the Editor lock, exact Unity version, result XML/log collection, repository-mutation checks, and scene/prefab inspection handoff.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It preserves the architecture’s valuable evidence boundaries while eliminating global canon invalidation, duplicated operational truth, speculative platform layers, and the missing crash-recovery semantics. It optimizes for repeated delivery of playable slices rather than exhaustive roadmap correctness.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The foundational principles are mostly sound: deterministic state outside model context, bounded workers, Git-based integration, immutable evidence, one worker initially, and Unity/runtime evidence that can override model confidence. The assembled system is nevertheless partially unsound as an autonomous development architecture. Its canonical scene identity is already split across GDD, task contracts, resource locks, tests, and current-state documentation; any GDD edit globally invalidates conformance; readiness and dispatch are disabled; and no durable execution/Git/Unity lifecycle joins planning to delivery. It is currently an audit platform, not a game-development accelerator.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: No current end-to-end gameplay ticket has traversed selection, implementation, Unity validation, repair, merge, and post-merge evidence, so actual time savings and human orchestration cost remain unmeasured. Availability and reliability of the Windows Unity host is the largest practical unknown.
do_not_build_yet: GitHub Projects dependency/status mirroring or bidirectional synchronization
Parallel workers, leases, merge queues, or generalized resource scheduling
A bundled Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority platform without a real blocking design artifact
More reconciliation auditor roles, streaming repair machinery, or full-game graph verification
Provider fallback or another provider transport layer
Incremental scanner/cache infrastructure beyond targeted rg/Git/Unity queries
Automatic merge or automatic evidence approval
Assignment 7/style integration until real authorized player-facing content needs it

evidence.observation: The frozen commit and working tree were confirmed as 9f2485dca1b61360e6d02810adc71e021346496e and clean before and after diagnostic commands.
The GDD declares the deleted Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity authoritative and calls Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity a non-canonical stub.
The actual builder, committed-scene tests, scene-location smoke test, conformance evidence, and CURRENT_STATE all treat Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity as authoritative.

Thirteen task resource claims reference the deleted old scene. A read-only scan found 36 concrete resource-path claims, 13 missing. NSC-037 explicitly requires registering the nonexistent scene and forbids using the actual authoritative one.

Despite that split brain, taskcontrol validate and the schema-v2 quality audit both report PASS; the independent scene-location smoke test also reports PASS. Each validates a locally consistent island but not cross-source authority.
The graph validator checks resource-key membership consistency but not whether concrete repo-file/unity-scene paths exist.
Conformance compares every record with the normalized hash of the entire GDD; any canon edit marks otherwise unchanged evidence stale.
Current history contains 13 GDD-changing commits with 466 added and 117 deleted lines, making moving-canon handling an experienced condition rather than a remote possibility.
taskcontrol validate passes, but taskcontrol ready reports readiness unavailable and zero authorized tasks. authorize always denies.

TaskExecution accepts caller-supplied task identity/hash, writes a wrapper artifact, and delegates one invocation. It does not resolve the contract from committed HEAD or implement task lifecycle, retries, Git, validation, or recovery.
Reconciliation emits taskcontrol_diff_required when Tasks exist, but the deterministic snapshot-to-contract diff/review/apply mechanism it calls for is not implemented.

Reconciliation current views and latest pointers are convenience copies written across multiple files without one atomic publication transaction; a crash can expose a mixed view, although immutable run directories limit historical damage.
Assignment 6 records two static-evaluator passes followed by Unity runtime failures and one no-op refinement before human-guided repair succeeded.

The current Unity gameplay remains a small door/mana/camera prototype; PlayerMovement still directly polls WASD. After Assignment 6, Assets history primarily contains camera test safety and scene-centralization changes rather than new player-facing systems.

A scale inspection counted approximately 31,384 non-output/non-JSON text lines under Pipeline, 3,283 task-contract lines, and 4,445 AI-pipeline documentation lines, versus about 1,595 C# lines under Assets/NoSafeCircle. This is a scale signal, not a productivity metric.
Production GDDRAG status and validation pass with 41 hash-current chunks, but integrity against the GDD cannot detect that the GDD’s canonical-scene claim is stale against Git.

NSC-023 currently derives as conformant from committed evidence. The human approval is represented only by a nonempty name and prose inside a repository JSON record, not an independently authenticated approval receipt.

gdd_iteration_concerns: A one-byte unrelated GDD change currently makes every delivered task that binds the document hash need revalidation.
Task contracts cite prose sections rather than stable requirement IDs/revisions, so scoped causal impact cannot be calculated deterministically.
The repository already demonstrates failure to propagate an engineering change—the canonical scene move—into the GDD, 22 task references, and resource groups.

Reconciliation is still framed primarily as global snapshot correctness. Routine iteration needs requirement-level change sets: added, modified, removed, clarified, and implementation-impact classification.
Existing planned work needs explicit outcomes after canon change: unaffected, needs_contract_revision, cancelled, superseded, implementation_migration_required, or revalidation_only.
Approved subordinate design artifacts need their own versioned requirement identities and dependency edges; merely hashing files recreates global invalidation at a smaller scale.
human_intervention_points: Choose the next player-visible slice and resolve ambiguous input, UX, architecture, and balance decisions.
Approve requirement/contract revisions and migration impact after material GDD changes.
Inspect scene, prefab, Input Actions, package, Build Settings, and serialized-reference changes.
Run or supervise experiential Play Mode checks for feel, framing, readability, timing, and visuals.
Review and merge PRs until automated delivery has a substantial successful track record.
Resolve repeated repairs, Unity host failures, merge conflicts, scope expansion, and budget exhaustion.
Approve generated design/art before it becomes canon and judge final game quality.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Exclusive-resource groups, leases, and future parallel-worker scheduling mostly protect against concurrency that is not yet enabled.
GitHub Issues/Projects mirroring, Draft-PR automation, and merge queues address future operational scale, not a current single-worker bottleneck.
Progressive decomposition and Artifact Authority protect against future missing-design invention; no production artifact flow currently demonstrates the need for the whole platform.

Extensive provider-polymorphism, malformed-container, Windows-path-alias, and fallback boundaries are valuable hardening but mostly protect future write-capable consumers; current providers are read-only for production work.
Full-game reconciliation with fifteen auditors and field-level streaming repair protects semantic bootstrap completeness, but ordinary feature delivery does not require repeating it.
Project-state caches and generic scanners target future token/latency savings; the current GDD and codebase remain small enough for bounded direct retrieval.
missing_components: One authoritative canonical-scene/project-state registry and a migration that updates GDD, tasks, locks, and build requirements together
Stable requirement IDs and scoped GDD impact/revision semantics
A legal operational transition table with compare-and-set rules, idempotency keys, retry ownership, and terminal states
A durable single-ticket attempt journal joining task, branch, commits, provider runs, validation, human decisions, PR, merge, and evidence
A contract resolver that verifies task revision/hash against committed HEAD rather than accepting caller assertions
A write-capable bounded gameplay execution path
A Windows Unity host adapter with Editor locking, exact-version checks, XML/log collection, timeout handling, and clean-tree verification
Deterministic reconciliation-to-task diff/review/apply tooling, if global reconciliation is retained
Git/GitHub projection reconciliation and crash-window handling
Measured delivery telemetry: elapsed time, model cost, human minutes, retries, Unity import/test time, and escaped defects

deliverables: First correct the canonical-scene split brain in one reviewed migration: GDD, affected task contracts, resource groups, NSC-037, and validation checks.
Deliver NSC-005 Player Mana reset and denied-cast feedback on one ordinary branch using a direct bounded coding worker; do not build a supervisor first.

Extend the existing PlayMode tests for reset, regeneration-delay reset, denied-spend signal, and readable low-mana feedback; run the clean Windows Unity wrapper and preserve XML/logs outside the repository.
Perform human Play Mode validation, merge, then create one post-merge delivery evidence manifest and record elapsed time, retries, cost, and human minutes.
Write the observed lifecycle as a tiny append-only run journal; implement coordinator code only for a failure that actually occurred during this slice.
next_slice.proof_of_value: Within one working day, NSC-005 is merged and demonstrably playable; clean Unity evidence is reproducible at the merged commit; the workflow can resume after one deliberately interrupted model invocation without duplicate commits or lost state; no more than two repair calls are needed; and human orchestration is measured rather than estimated.
next_slice.title: Repair authority drift, then ship NSC-005 through a no-new-platform delivery lane
next_slice.why: NSC-005 extends existing runtime code and PlayMode tests without Input Actions, package changes, or scene-builder ownership. It exercises implementation, feedback, Unity validation, repair, merge, and evidence while avoiding NSC-003’s unresolved control semantics and the stale scene locks. It is the fastest honest test of whether the pipeline saves development time.

observed_failure_solutions: Runtime evidence re-entering GER directly addresses the two camera implementations that passed static review but failed in Unity.
The no-op progress guard and bounded circuit breaker address the recorded Refiner claim of implementation without an Assets change.
The clean Unity runner and non-saving test seams address prior test-process waiting, repository-mutation, and canonical-scene safety problems reflected in repository history.

Immutable reconciliation runs, resume utilities, deterministic finding IDs, and conflict handling address actual max-turn, recovery, identity, and merge defects encountered while bootstrapping reconciliation.
The production GDDRAG integrity boundary addresses the historical Assignment 4 index becoming stale after substantial GDD revision.
Provider-scoped immutable ArchitectureReview runs and AgentRuntime normalization solve real audit-workflow provenance, timeout, and provider-output transport needs, though not gameplay delivery.
overengineering: The project built an exhaustive 37-contract graph, multi-model reconciliation, recovery layers, streaming field repair, provider abstraction, and architecture-review migration before one current gameplay ticket could be dispatched.

Fifteen reconciliation auditors produced 56 first-pass findings and required bespoke refinement/conflict tooling. That improved bootstrap quality but is disproportionate for a rolling single-developer gameplay backlog.
Task resource claims are duplicated again in RESOURCE_GROUPS.yaml; exact agreement is validated, but existence and current ownership are not.
TaskExecution duplicates the full invocation in task_request.json while AgentRuntime publishes request.json separately, without a transaction joining their completion.
Provider trust-boundary hardening is much deeper than the missing vertical delivery path: repository writing, Git, Unity, task selection, and recovery remain absent.
Current/LATEST reconciliation views add several mutable projections whose authority must continually be explained.

The planned Milestone 2 bundles RAG, scanner, context packs, decomposition, artifact authority, generation, GER, and promotion despite CURRENT_STATE correctly warning against building most of it speculatively.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary separation: GDD/design authority, task definition, integrated Git state, validation evidence, transient execution, and human approval should remain distinct.

The GDD currently contains mutable repository-location and pipeline-operation facts. Those belong in an engineering/project-state registry referenced by design requirements, not duplicated as game-design canon.

Tasks contain historical repository evidence and stale concrete paths while current Git and conformance evidence say something else; bootstrap observations are being mistaken for durable integration contracts.
Task resource ownership is stored in task files and RESOURCE_GROUPS.yaml. One should be derived from the other.
Future GitHub state must be a projection of one operational ledger. If both are writable authorities, claim, retry, close, and merge races become ambiguous.
Conformance surfaces are manually enumerated. Omitted dependencies can change without invalidating evidence, producing false conformance; unrelated listed files can produce needless revalidation.
A plain approved_by string inside a repository record is an approval assertion, not authenticated human authority unless protected review/merge policy supplies that authority externally.
The transition from merged code to a later committed evidence record has no owned crash-recovery receipt. A merge can succeed while the task remains not_delivered indefinitely.
AgentRuntime run directories are immutable but incomplete directories after interruption are not resumable under the same run ID; a higher coordinator must classify and reconcile these orphans.
CURRENT_STATE and START_HERE contain mutually stale milestone directions and readiness claims, weakening the repository-as-truth principle.
strong_decisions: Models do not own durable state or declare their own success.
Integrated Git state is distinguished from model claims and builder capability.
Task definition is separated from mutable operational/completion state.
Deterministic validation precedes expensive semantic review where practical.
Unity/runtime evidence can override a static evaluator pass.
Normal tests must not mutate canonical Unity assets, and clean-tree state is part of validation.
One worker precedes parallelism; branches/worktrees protect main.
Reconciliation history is immutable and cannot directly rewrite task contracts.
Missing design is escalated rather than silently invented.
Retries and repair loops are bounded, and no-op repair consumes budget.
Generic provider invocation is separated from No Safe Circle task identity.
structural_flaws: Canonical-scene authority is already contradictory across root canon, tasks, resource locks, actual assets, tests, and evidence. The validators all pass because no cross-boundary invariant covers it.
Whole-document canon hashing makes synchronization with iterative design equivalent to global revalidation.

There is no operational state machine connecting active contract, readiness, claim, attempt, validation, human review, merge, delivery evidence, dependency satisfaction, retry, cancellation, or recovery.

The architecture specifies Git branches, worktrees, GitHub Issues/PRs, and leases without defining idempotent external side effects, compare-and-set ownership, duplicate-event handling, or restart reconciliation.
Current schema 2.0 removed unsafe status but did not replace it with dependency-satisfaction semantics; the graph therefore cannot answer the question it was built to answer.
The reconciliation-to-task delta boundary is a documented call to an unimplemented tool.
TaskExecution does not prove that its supplied contract identity is current or approved.
Manual conformance-surface selection cannot prove completeness of the change-impact boundary.
Mutable convenience views and pointers are not atomically published as one generation, allowing mixed current views after interruption.
Documentation routing has accumulated incompatible current plans, so agents cannot safely infer the active architecture from START_HERE and milestone files alone.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: Major near-term leverage is not currently plausible. The frozen system authorizes zero tasks and lacks repository-write, Git, Unity-host, merge, and recovery orchestration. Since the historical GER camera delivery, infrastructure expanded far more than playable code, and the first post-bootstrap engineering change already desynchronized canon and task state. The bounded-agent/GER approach can plausibly speed individual coding and repair, as the camera experiment suggests, but “days instead of weeks” requires repeated measured deliveries. Until two or three real slices complete through the same thin lane, the architecture is producing safety documentation and audit leverage—not development throughput.
structured_output.verdict_reason: Do not discard the core principles, but reject the current milestone sequence and state model. The architecture is not fundamentally wrong in choosing deterministic ownership and bounded workers; it is partially unsound because its moving-canon semantics, canonical-resource authority, lifecycle transitions, and recovery boundaries fail under conditions the repository has already experienced. Reorganize around a small requirement-versioned delivery ledger and a real Unity vertical slice before adding more infrastructure.
